questions.q: Let one observation equal to the mean is added to $n$ observations. If the variance changes from $78$ to $72$, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Adding mean to the observations does not change the value of $∑ {\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}$, hence,

$\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}}{n}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n + 1}{\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}}{n + 1}\right)} = \dfrac{78}{72}$
$⇒ \dfrac{n + 1}{n} = \dfrac{78}{72} ⇒ n = 12$

questions.q: If the variance of the first $n$ natural numbers is $10$ and the variance of the first $m$ even natural numbers is $16,$ then the value of  $m + n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$var\left(1, 2, \ldots n\right) = 10 ⇒ \dfrac{{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + \ldots + {n}^{2}}{n} - {\left(\dfrac{1 + 2 + \ldots + n}{n}\right)}^{2} = 10$
$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{6} - {\left(\dfrac{n + 1}{2}\right)}^{2} = 10$
$⇒ {n}^{2} - 1 = 120 ⇒ n = 11$
$var\left(2, 4, 6 \ldots . , 2m\right) = 16 ⇒ var\left(1, 2 \ldots . , m\right) = 4$
$⇒ {m}^{2} - 1 = 48 ⇒ m = 7 ⇒ m + n = 18$
